description: The reading half of the Instagram account: the comments and the direct messages, the answer that goes out on its own, the lead that becomes a ticket, and the numbers the post creator writes with
client_copy: Lee los comentarios y los mensajes de tu Instagram, contesta los que puede contestar solo, te deja en el tablero los que tenés que ver vos y te marca a los que son clientes.
_comment: PUBLISHING IS NOT HERE AND IS NOT MOVING. `social/core/instagram.py` puts
a post on the account and this plugin reads what people say under it: two
halves of one connection, two plugins, because a client buys either one on
its own. What they share is the TOKEN, and they share it by name —
`engine.provide('instagram.token', ...)` — never by importing each other's
module: every enabled plugin's surface modules live in ONE sys.modules
namespace and load in CORE_PLUGINS order, so an import would be a bet on
who got there first. That is also why every module in here is prefixed
THE ENV IS THE SEED AND THE TABLE IS THE CURRENT TOKEN. IG_ACCESS_TOKEN
comes from the instance's secrets.env, which is outside the container: a
refreshed token is written into `instagram_account` and every Graph call
reads the table first. Before that, a refresh lived in one process's
os.environ and died with it, which is how a connection that refreshes
itself still expires after sixty days.
IG_USERNAME IS NOT AN ENV. It is a fact about the token, read once from
GET /me and cached next to it, and it is what tells the account's own
replies apart from a stranger's -- Instagram hands ours back nested under
the comment they answer, and an agent that read its own reply as new would
answer itself every fifteen minutes.
READING IS A FLOW AND NOT A LOOP. `flows/instagram` ticks every fifteen
minutes, and a tick with nothing new is two tool calls and one line. The
engine's loader copies the FLOW.md into workspace/flows/ when the plugin
loads if it is not there, and never overwrites: from the moment the file exists it is
the client's, hers to pause and the agent's to edit. It was
`comentarios-instagram` until 16/9/2026, and the rename is handled the only
honest way a rename can be: an installed copy that is byte for byte the one
we shipped is retired, anything else is left alone and said out loud in the
log (`core/plugin.py`'s SUPERSEDED).
THE DMs ARE IN, AND THE `Advanced Access` STORY WAS WRONG for this flavor.
Probed on our own account with the token we already had: GET
/v21.0/me/conversations?platform=instagram answers {"data": []}, not a
permission error. Standard Access is enough for an account whose owner has
a role in our Meta app -- the same rule publishing lives under -- and what
Advanced Access buys is the same thing it buys there: any client connecting
with a button instead of a developer-console invite. What DOES gate it is
the client's: a professional account, and «Permitir acceso a mensajes» on
in the Instagram app, a consumer setting no dashboard can see.
THE FIELDS ARE THE DOCUMENTED ONES. A conversation is `id` and
`updated_time` (no `participants` on this flavor) and a message is
`id,created_time,from,to,message` (no `attachments`): a field Graph does
not know fails the whole call, so who is in a thread is read off the
messages, where `from` is {username, id} and that id is the IGSID a reply
is addressed to. Sending is the one call that is JSON with a Bearer header
and not a form: POST /{IG_USER_ID}/messages.
AND MESSAGES HAVE A CLOCK: Meta allows an answer up to 24 hours after the
person's last message, and every message of theirs starts it again. The
window is in the listing, so the threads about to close go first, and it is
checked in the tool body before anything is sent.
ANSWERS GO OUT WITHOUT THE CLIENT'S YES since 24/9/2026 (Luis): a comment
or a DM is a person waiting, and a reply parked in Aprobaciones is a lead
going cold. What the gate did around them the tools do now: the words that
went out in Activity, the ticket closed with them. What is not the agent's
to answer is decided by `skills/comments`, and goes to the board instead.
IT REQUIRES `approval` AND `kanban`: hiding a comment is still gated, which
needs the approval plugin's row, card and queue; and a comment that reads
like a lead becomes a ticket
on the board, which is the kanban plugin's `create_ticket` with
source=instagram and the comment id as source_ref -- that pair is the
dedupe, so the same comment never opens two.
